title: Package declarations contain syntax and duplicate identifier blockers
issue: The no_parent_attr_name PRAGMA at line 50 contains an extra comma. Repeated exception declarations include invalid_parameter, crud_unknown, idx_internal_check and others. References to repeated names are ambiguous.
impact: The supplied main body cannot compile as delivered. Runtime findings are conditional on resolving build errors.
proposal: First agree one error-code map, remove duplicate declarations, repair the PRAGMA, and compile the entire unit. Do not select an error number merely because it occurs last.
test: Compile the unchanged baseline and capture USER_ERRORS; after an agreed correction, require zero errors. Review each public error-code compatibility change.

title: Persistence contract differs from the supplied base table
issue: CRUD writes TNS_ALIAS, PHASE, HOST_NAME and other columns into ADMIN_TNSNAMES_BASE. The supplied base table contains only BASE_PK and TNS_ID.
impact: Dynamic INSERT/UPDATE fails at runtime against this DDL; fixing package syntax alone does not restore registration.
proposal: Concept decision required: keep the current attribute hierarchy and make registration persist one complete entry atomically through it. The alternative is a wide-table migration; it is not an equivalent drop-in fix.
test: Install only declared dependencies in a test schema, then register and update one alias; verify every persisted node and its parent.

title: Reference table constraint names an absent column
issue: The STATUS check constraint reads MANDATORY, which is not a column of ADMIN_TNSNAMES_REFERENCE. MANDATORY belongs to the attributes table.
impact: CREATE TABLE fails and prevents dependent objects from being created.
proposal: Concept: separate reference support status from attribute requiredness. Select the allowed STATUS set independently; do not add a copied MANDATORY column without a functional reason.
test: Create the reference table alone in Oracle 19c; test each allowed and rejected status and then the attribute foreign key.

title: View and helper queries use an older checks-table contract
issue: The view selects TNS_ATTR_CHECK, TNS_ATTR_STATEMENT and TNS_ATTR_CHECK_TYPE. The supplied table defines CHECK_TARGET, CHECK_STATEMENT and CHECK_TYPE instead. Standalone validation functions also use the old names.
impact: The view and helpers cannot compile against the supplied table. This is direct contract drift, not proof that every differently dated component is incompatible.
proposal: Choose the installed contract explicitly; update all consumers together. The three column-name substitutions alone do not validate the view grammar or its return types.
test: Create the baseline table and compile each consumer separately; record all invalid objects, then test ATTRIBUTE and VALUE rule lookup.

title: Installation prerequisites and runnable scripts are not isolated
issue: SLICE_CLOB, the staging table and ADMIN_TNSNAMES_AUDIT are referenced but not defined by an installation contract in this ZIP. The view calls an unqualified standalone validator while the supplied implementation is packaged and returns a collection. The FUNCTION and SQL files mix definitions, experiments and sample DML.
impact: A clean installation is not reproducible. Existing standalone objects may hide missing dependencies. Running the experimental files as installers can change data.
proposal: Create a reviewed object/grant/version inventory and explicit installation order. Separate samples from installable components; inventory existing standalone functions and SQL types before choosing the view adapter.
test: Install in an isolated schema from a reviewed list; inspect USER_OBJECTS, USER_ERRORS and USER_DEPENDENCIES. Do not run the scratch scripts as a batch.

title: Definer-rights CRUD exposes an unchecked mutation route
issue: CRUD is public in an AUTHID DEFINER package. It does not call the access/maintenance gate and reads continue without enforcing it. PROTO intake compares roles but does not enforce administrator/contributor flags before DDL/DML.
impact: An EXECUTE grantee could reach mutation without the intended application check once runtime contracts are repaired. Actual grants and exploitability are not inspected.
proposal: Keep the documented public interface until callers are inventoried, but enforce a shared fail-closed gate at every public mutation boundary. Prefer private persistence routines in a future agreed interface revision.
test: Use EXECUTE-only users with no configured role, contributor role and administrator role. Direct CRUD and intake must reject unauthorised requests before any mutation.

title: SQL text concatenates unescaped values
issue: Alias, description and other JSON strings are concatenated into SQL literals. Numeric text is also rendered into statement text.
impact: A description such as OBrien breaks SQL; malicious values may alter the SQL structure. The code runs with definer rights.
proposal: After selecting the target table model, bind every data value with native dynamic SQL or use static DML. Keep dynamic SQL only where required; do not replace binding with quote removal.
test: Test apostrophes, Unicode, NULL, boundary lengths and hostile quote text. Assert exact stored values and unchanged unrelated rows.

title: Description is lost between JSON producer and consumer
issue: REGISTER_TNS emits the key description. CRUD reads entry_description.
impact: A valid supplied description becomes NULL in persistence.
proposal: Use one documented JSON contract with typed extraction and required-key validation. Preserve the public parameter name.
test: Register and update an alias with a nonempty description and verify the value end to end. Also distinguish an omitted update field from an explicit clear.

title: Date default depends on NLS conversion
issue: The VARCHAR2 parameter p_date_valid_from defaults to SYSDATE. That conversion uses the session date format, but CRUD parses it with YYYY-MM-DD.
impact: Calls that omit the date can fail or interpret it incorrectly under other NLS settings.
proposal: Preserve the string interface for compatibility; use an explicit ISO default and FX validation, or propose a typed DATE overload with documented time-of-day policy. Do not silently truncate dates.
test: Repeat omitted and explicit dates under DD-MON-RR and YYYY-MM-DD. Include leap days and invalid calendar dates.

title: Staging query and cleanup are not scoped to the intake
issue: The validation query reads ADMIN_TNSNAMES_PROTO_CHECKS without filtering the current proto ID. INSERT assigns the current ID even when the fetched row comes from another intake. Cleanup deletes all staging rows.
impact: Concurrent or leftover staging rows can be reassigned or deleted. Impact depends on whether TEMP_TNSNAMES_PROTO_ENTRIES is permanent or session-private; its DDL is absent.
proposal: Make request ownership explicit; filter validation and cleanup by the allocated proto ID. Confirm staging lifetime first. Use session-local collections or a precreated GTT if consistent with the design.
test: Two sessions submit distinct aliases concurrently; add leftover rows. Verify no cross-request reads, inserts or deletes. Repeat a second call in one session.

title: Shared sequence DDL introduces contention and transaction boundaries
issue: Each call creates and drops the same permanent ordering sequence. CREATE PRIVATE TEMPORARY TABLE uses PRESERVE DEFINITION, whose creation commits in Oracle 19c. An explicit COMMIT precedes evaluate_entry. MAX+1 is calculated but overwritten by a sequence value.
impact: Concurrent calls can interfere with the shared sequence. Caller work can be committed before entry acceptance, and later rollback cannot undo committed intake.
proposal: Concept: remove per-request permanent DDL; allocate identity once with the existing persistent sequence and derive request-local positions deterministically. Keep validation and registration in a caller-owned transaction unless an explicit service contract says otherwise.
test: Insert an unrelated marker without committing, call intake, then roll back. Verify the marker and intake atomicity; repeat with evaluation failure and concurrent calls.

title: Dynamic execution helpers hide failures
issue: EXEC_DSQL prints SQLERRM but does not re-raise. Several outer handlers notify and return. TNSNAMES_STATUS can leave p_cont unset after handled errors.
impact: Failure can look like success and later steps can run after unsuccessful setup. Output is not a reliable failure contract.
proposal: Propagate operational errors after cleanup; preserve the original error if cleanup also fails. Initialise outputs to a rejected state before work. Keep expected business rejections explicit.
test: Inject table/sequence/privilege failures at each stage. Require a raised error, no false accepted status, and preservation of original diagnostics.

title: Intake changes user content before validation
issue: REGEXP_REPLACE removes commas, question marks, angle brackets and other characters from every split line before validating it.
impact: Distinct inputs collapse to the same text; alias lists and values can be altered. Lossless reconstruction and trustworthy canonicalisation are impossible from this altered representation.
proposal: Retain original text and source offsets. Reject unsupported syntax with a location; apply only grammar-defined whitespace handling. Normalisation must follow successful parsing.
test: Test multiple aliases, punctuation in a quoted value, comments and invalid syntax. Require either preserved meaning or a precise rejection; never silent deletion.

title: Invalid lines can disappear before acceptance
issue: The view filters INVALID_ATTRIBUTE and inner-joins known checks. evaluate_entry validates only rows that survived intake. It does not prove that all input tokens were consumed, required nodes exist, or parentheses balance.
impact: An accepted subset does not prove the complete descriptor is valid. An FK proves attribute membership, not grammar correctness.
proposal: Make complete input consumption, balanced nesting, required children and cardinality explicit acceptance conditions. Keep rejected tokens in diagnostic output.
test: Add an unknown attribute to an otherwise valid descriptor; remove CONNECT_DATA or a closing bracket. All must be rejected as complete entries.

title: PROTO persistence drops node identity and sequence
issue: The final proto table stores TNS_ATTR and TNS_ATTR_VALUE but no parent instance, node ID or input position. The attributes table has a definition hierarchy; it does not by itself identify each repeated instance in an input descriptor.
impact: Repeated ADDRESS/HOST nodes cannot be reconstructed reliably from the stored proto rows alone. JSON_ARRAYAGG also has no explicit ordering.
proposal: Keep definition hierarchy and instance hierarchy distinct. Preserve node ID, parent node ID and sibling position; normalise only unordered properties. Use the same typed node model for generation and comparison.
test: Round-trip two DESCRIPTION nodes each with two addresses and differing values. Verify exact parentage, sibling order and diagnostic source positions.

title: CLOB input is narrowed to several VARCHAR2 buffers
issue: The input CLOB is inserted into VARCHAR2(4000). Fetch buffers for lines/values are VARCHAR2(64), and v_json is VARCHAR2(2000). JSON aggregation defaults to VARCHAR2(4000).
impact: Long descriptors or values can fail before reporting despite the CLOB public interface.
proposal: Use a CLOB-safe tokenisation path and explicit bounds per field. Generate large JSON with RETURNING CLOB at each relevant aggregation/object layer. Define limits rather than relying on implicit conversion.
test: Test 65-character host/value, 2048-character values and descriptors above 4000 and 32767 bytes, including multibyte text. Require correct results or explicit documented size rejection.

title: Re-evaluation never clears a prior acceptance
issue: evaluate_entry sets INTAKE_ENTRY_ACCEPTED to Y only for accepted entries. It does not write N when validation fails. It counts existing row flags rather than checking expected structure.
impact: An entry previously marked Y can remain accepted after its flags become invalid.
proposal: Concept: compute the entire decision once, reject empty input and persist Y or N for the entire request atomically, with validation version and time.
test: Accept an entry, change one flag to N, evaluate again and require every row to show N. Test zero rows and mixed flags.

title: Duplicate alias matches are treated as absence
issue: Both existence checks map COUNT=1 to Y and all other counts to N. Existing rows are pivoted with MAX and the retrieval joins on alias text.
impact: Duplicate registrations can trigger another create instead of a diagnostic. Multi-address values collapse to one MAX value; ambiguity can overwrite OUT parameters.
proposal: Resolve distinct registration IDs first. Return absent, unique or ambiguous explicitly; enforce the agreed alias/phase identity transactionally. Query the hierarchy for all address instances rather than pivoting them into a scalar.
test: Supply zero, one and two matching registrations and repeated addresses. Require a deterministic unique result or an explicit ambiguity error, never create-on-duplicate.

title: Audit updates miss transitions involving NULL
issue: Update logging requires NEW IS NOT NULL and NEW <> OLD. Clearing a value fails the first condition; NULL-to-value makes the comparison UNKNOWN.
impact: Audit history omits valid changes and cannot support reliable rollback/reconstruction of those changes.
proposal: Use a null-safe change predicate for each typed field; preserve raw old/new values. Review delete code that uppercases values separately from actual stored content.
test: Test NULL-to-value, value-to-NULL, unchanged NULL, equal non-NULL and changed non-NULL for each audited field.

title: Per-attribute trigger creates unrelated base registrations
issue: The entries row trigger creates a new base row for every inserted attribute and does not use that generated ID for the supplied NEW.TNS_ID. It references ADMIN_TNSNAMES_BASE_TNSID_SEQ while the DDL defines ADMIN_TNSNAMES_TNSID_SEQ.
impact: With missing dependencies fixed, attribute insertion can create orphan base rows or fail. Registration identity allocation is duplicated across layers.
proposal: Allocate one TNS_ID at the registration boundary, persist its base row once and attach all attribute nodes to it. Let audit triggers record changes, not allocate separate registrations.
test: Insert an entry of ten nodes; require one base row and all ten nodes with its ID. Roll back and verify both base and nodes disappear.

title: Port validation accepts non-port numeric strings
issue: The numeric regex allows periods and checks neither integerness nor the full 1..65535 interval. The 1520..1600 test has warning severity, so values outside it need not stop processing.
impact: 0, 65536 and decimal values can pass the hard numeric gate. Period-only or repeated-period strings can produce conversion failures.
proposal: Separate valid TCP-port syntax/range from local preferred-port policy. Require a non-NULL integer in 1..65535; keep the preferred range as a documented warning if intended.
test: Test NULL, 0, 1, 1521, 65535, 65536, -1, 1.5 and dotted strings. Confirm the local-policy warning does not redefine protocol validity.

title: Generated template and documented call do not match the API
issue: The generated sample calls register_tns(l_clob), but the specification exposes a multi-parameter routine, not that overload. A multirow UNION query is selected into a scalar; template strings include DESCIPTION and an unclosed SERVER component.
impact: Users cannot copy the generated sample into a working registration flow. The procedure prints a template; it is not a working descriptor serialiser.
proposal: Choose the intended typed or PROTO intake route explicitly. Generate a complete valid sample for that route, including concatenation/aggregation and stable ordering; validate the sample as part of release checks.
test: Copy the printed example into a clean Oracle 19c client. Require successful compilation, valid balanced descriptor and the expected target routine.

title: Normalisation principles transfer; existing parser code does not yet
issue: The module already separates reference documentation, attribute definitions, validation rules and instance values. However, the PROTO path lacks a lossless instance tree, canonical encoding, versioned normalisation and fingerprint generation.
impact: It is useful design input for ADMIN_OBJECTS, but it is not a proven canonical manifest engine. Copying the current parser would transfer its data-loss and ordering defects.
proposal: Retain separate domain extractors. Reuse the rule/definition/value separation, explicit ordering concept and diagnostic model. Specify a common typed serialisation contract only after the two domains pass golden tests. No shared utility package is justified yet.
test: Run equivalent-format and unequal-meaning cases in both domains. Require identical bytes only for agreed equivalence, and a mismatch for semantically relevant changes. See the comparison document.

title: Current ADMIN_OBJECTS hash path is different from the proposed manifest
issue: The locally available ADMIN_OBJECTS body hashes v_metadata with STANDARD_HASH(..., MD5). It does not implement the profile/object-manifest design discussed in Oracle tabelstructuur vergelijken. This is a dated local reference, not a claim about deployed code.
impact: There is no existing pair of canonical generators that can simply be merged. Directly hashing arbitrary CLOB input with STANDARD_HASH is unsupported.
proposal: Use the chat design as concept context. Pin profile ID/version, format version, algorithm and byte encoding; use a LOB-safe hash implementation such as DBMS_CRYPTO with explicit conversion where needed. Preserve expected-baseline provenance and report incomplete extraction separately from mismatch.
test: Compare canonical bytes and SHA-256 for shuffled irrelevant properties, changed key-column order, multibyte text, NULL and large manifests. Do not treat local illustrative tests as Oracle execution.

title: Validation output can overwrite the accumulated decision
issue: VALIDATE_TNS records decisions in its validation array but exports v_continue from the last validation call. PORT_CHECKER can overwrite the hostname result instead of exporting the final accumulated array decision.
impact: A later successful port check can obscure a prior failure if execution reaches it. Several business handlers also return without an explicit final rejected flag.
proposal: Derive the final outcome from one cumulative decision. Initialise rejection before validation and set acceptance only when every required check completed successfully.
test: Force a hostname rejection followed by a valid port and require rejection. Test every handled exception and NULL output path.

title: Preference helper reads ADMIN_SESSION configuration
issue: GET_PREF types and queries ADMIN_SESSIONS_PREFS, while TNSNAMES_STATUS uses ADMIN_TNSNAMES_PREFS.
impact: A public helper has an unexpected cross-module dependency and may return another modules value. Intended shared policy is not documented.
proposal: Confirm whether this is a copied dependency or an intentional shared preference API. Prefer module-local configuration for TNS-specific settings; preserve deliberate shared configuration through an explicit contract.
test: Set distinct values under the same key in both preference tables and verify the selected contract. Verify the package can compile with declared prerequisites only.

title: PROTO validator contains an invalid aggregate projection
issue: The nested SELECT projects attr alongside COUNT(*) without GROUP BY. The outer BULK COLLECT return is a collection, while the supplied view expects scalar attribute fields from an unqualified helper.
impact: The supplied packaged validator has an additional static SQL blocker and its interface is not interchangeable with the view call.
proposal: Define whether validation returns one typed result or a collection. Use a direct REGEXP_LIKE decision for one input; implement the SQL-visible adapter only if the view requires it. Do not assume a packaged collection is a SQL object.
test: Compile the PROTO body and SQL-visible consumer independently; test matching, nonmatching and NULL values and check the exact return type.
